apiConnections.title: Turn your data sources into secure REST APIs
apiConnections.description: Generate a REST API from a database, file store, remote service, or script, then test it and lock it down before you hand it off. Everything you need to build and ship an API lives here.
apiConnections.apiTypesText: Generate a REST API from a database, file store, remote service, or script. DreamFactory builds and secures the endpoints for you.
apiConnections.apiBuilderText: Compose your existing services into one custom API with multiple endpoints and your own logic.
apiConnections.apiDocsText: Read the generated OpenAPI reference and try live calls right in the browser.
apiConnections.dataExplorerText: Browse records and confirm your filters, fields, and relationships return the data you expect.
apiConnections.eventScriptsText: Run your own logic before or after a request to validate input, reshape responses, or trigger side effects.
apiConnections.rolesText: Control which services, tables, and endpoints each user, app, or agent is allowed to reach.
apiConnections.keysText: Issue an application key for each caller and bind it to the role it should run as.
apiConnections.noteSecureTitle: Lock it down before you share
apiConnections.noteSecureText: A generated API stays open until a role and an API key say who can call it. Set both before you hand out the URL.
apiConnections.noteTestText: Confirm the shape and data of a new API in API Docs or Data Explorer before sharing any credentials.
apiConnections.noteConnectorsText: The API types you can generate depend on the connectors installed in this DreamFactory build.

apiTypes.title: Pick the source you want to expose
apiTypes.description: DreamFactory turns databases, file stores, remote services, scripts, and platform utilities into secured REST APIs. Choose the source type that matches the system you want to connect.
apiTypes.apiBuilderText: Compose your existing services into one custom API with multiple endpoints and your own logic.
apiTypes.databaseText: Generate a REST API from a SQL or big-data database, complete with tables, views, stored procedures, filtering, and relationships.
apiTypes.scriptingText: Expose custom server-side logic as an endpoint when a direct connector is not enough.
apiTypes.networkText: Wrap and govern a remote HTTP or SOAP service so it runs through DreamFactory security.
apiTypes.fileText: Serve files and object storage over REST with the same permissions as the rest of your APIs.
apiTypes.utilityText: Add platform services like email, cache, notifications, and logging to support your APIs.
apiTypes.noteGatewayText: Each source type connects DreamFactory to a different class of system, but they all become REST APIs with the same shape.
apiTypes.noteGovernanceText: Roles, API keys, scripting, and docs all apply the same way once the source API exists.
apiTypes.noteInstalledText: Source types with no installed connector are marked unavailable in this instance.

security.title: Control who can call your APIs
security.description: Decide how callers prove who they are and what each one is allowed to reach. Authentication, rate limits, roles, and application keys all live here.
security.authText: Let users sign in through LDAP, SSO, OAuth, or another installed provider.
security.rateText: Cap how many calls a user, role, service, IP, or key can make so no single client can overwhelm your APIs.
security.rolesText: Define exactly which services, tables, and endpoints each caller can reach.
security.keysText: Review your application keys and the role each one grants to callers.
security.notePrivilegeText: Give a new role the narrowest access that works, then widen it only when an app or user actually needs more.
security.noteLimitsText: Limits keep a runaway or abusive client from overwhelming an expensive or sensitive API.
security.noteProvidersText: The sign-in options you see reflect the authentication connectors installed in this instance.

lookupKeys.label: Lookup Keys
lookupKeys.desc: Lookup keys for service configuration and credentials must be made private.
lookupKeys.fullDesc: The DreamFactory administrator can create any number of 'key, value' pairs attached to a role. The key values are automatically substituted on the server. For example, key names can be used in the username and password fields required to hook up a SQL or NoSQL database. They can also be used in Email Templates or as parameters for external REST services. Any Lookup Key can be marked as private, and in this case the key value is securely encrypted on the server and is no longer accessible through the platform interface. Lookup keys for service configuration and credentials must be made private.
